clue.text: One helps to define the goal of angry lawyers

definitions.text: One helps to define the goal

parts.note: the Bar is the collective name for barristers, the legal profession

explanation.surface: A sporting aim seems to be set by a group of furious solicitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The goal of angry lawyers' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'goal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The horizontal beam across the top of football or rugby posts marks the limits of the scoring target.

clue.text: Come to an end — like someone's innings?

definitions.meaning: to be used up or exhausted, as supplies do
in cricket a batsman's innings can finish when he is dismissed short of his ground while running

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator wonders whether a batter's stay at the crease is over.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter is dismissed this way when the fielders break the wicket before the batter completes a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are exhausted have finished; a cricket dismissal of this kind ends a batter's innings.

clue.text: Well-kept public transport to get backing

indicators.note: to get backing here means the word is turned to run backwards

parts.note: trams are street railway cars, a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A tidy city tram network seeks funding support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get backing' sounds like winning financial support; here it turns TRAMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat and well maintained looks trim and tidy, a common sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Glass or beer-mat needs changing

indicators.note: something that needs changing will be rearranged, so the letters of the preceding words are reordered

explanation.surface: In a pub, either your pint glass or the coaster under it needs replacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass' looks like a drinking vessel beside the beer-mat, but it is the old word for a weather instrument; OR plus BEERMAT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A weather glass is a traditional name for the instrument that measures atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Ruth Rendell's first English detective

definitions.note: ruth is an old word for sorrow or pity, surviving in 'ruthless'

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the crime writer's name

parts.note: Inspector Morse is Colin Dexter's famous Oxford detective

explanation.surface: Seems to name the first English sleuth created by crime novelist Ruth Rendell.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth Rendell's detective was Wexford, but 'Ruth' is the definition: an archaic word for regret. Morse is another writer's detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic ruth means sorrow or regret for wrongdoing, the same feeling of contrition and guilt.

clue.text: I eat outside in German city

indicators.note: outside means the eating word goes around the letter I

parts.note: to munch is to eat steadily

explanation.surface: A traveller reports dining al fresco in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat outside' suggests an outdoor meal, but 'outside' places MUNCH around I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian capital is a major city in southern Germany, famous for Oktoberfest.

clue.text: Hyperactive chap in charge

explanation.surface: A frantic, overactive fellow is running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wildly energetic and overexcited is described as frenzied in this way.

clue.text: What a fisherman actually gains from his work?

definitions.text: What a fisherman actually gains from his work?

parts.words: What a fisherman actually gains from his work?
parts.note: a fisherman's mesh brings in his haul, and the clue puns on the accounting term for earnings after costs

explanation.surface: Asks what an angler really earns from his labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actually gains' is the business sense: takings after expenses. The fisherman's mesh supplies the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The accounting term for income left after deducting all costs, punning on a fishing mesh.

clue.text: Transference of money?

parts.note: a current is a flow, so a flow of money is its circulation; the word is also the general term for money itself

explanation.surface: Reads like a banking term for moving funds between accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both circulation, the passing of something from hand to hand, and the money that circulates.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in use as a medium of exchange, and the state of circulating from person to person.

clue.text: It's not just a mixture of fun and music

indicators.note: a mixture of the letters means they are stirred into a new order

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A cocktail of fun and music is more than mere entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not just' reads as 'it is more than', but 'not just' means unjust. FUN mixed gives UNF.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust treatment lacks fairness or equity, so the two expressions are synonyms.

clue.text: Room isn't fitted for display units

indicators.note: fitted means put together or assembled, so the letters are arranged into a new word

explanation.surface: An office has not been fitted out for the screens it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitted' signals rearranging ROOM ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer screens are units that display output, so they are examples of the definition.

clue.text: Maybe more cuts will attract one

definitions.note: the pronoun stands for a single shopper drawn in by price cuts

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters are just one possible arrangement, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A retailer hopes that further price reductions will draw in a shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue nearly defines the answer: more price cuts attract a shopper, who is the 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'one' attracted by lower prices is a shopper or buyer at a store.

clue.text: Where seconds do the work of a minute

definitions.text: Where seconds do the work of a minute

parts.words: Where seconds do the work of a minute
parts.note: in boxing a fighter's seconds tend him during the one-minute break between rounds, in his allotted spot of the ring

explanation.surface: Sounds like a riddle about time, with seconds doing a minute's job.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds are a boxer's assistants, not units of time; they work during the minute's rest between rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's assistants work at his station in the ring between rounds of the fight.

clue.text: It's strictly true, but unimaginative

definitions.meaning: as a noun phrase, something that is an actual fact rather than opinion
as an adjective, prosaic and down-to-earth in manner

explanation.surface: Describes a statement that is accurate but dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun phrase means a plain fact; hyphenated as an adjective it means prosaic and unemotional.

clue.text: Growing row over speaker?

parts.note: a row of hair growing above the mouth, the 'speaker'

explanation.surface: Suggests an escalating argument about a loudspeaker or the House of Commons Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' is a line of hair, not a quarrel, and the 'speaker' is the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair grown on the upper lip forms a line above the mouth.

clue.text: Prevails in arranging some cover

indicators.note: arranging the words means placing their letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wins through by organising some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' rearranges SOME COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is to win or triumph over opposition, the same as defeating it.

clue.text: Pass on information that's personal

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to hint or make known indirectly
as an adjective, private and close

explanation.surface: Telling someone something private.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the adjective are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hint or suggest; the adjective means private or closely familiar.

clue.text: Private eye puts query in novel to a male

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is a man

explanation.surface: A fictional detective slips a question into a book addressed to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal for QUERY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A private detective, in old-fashioned British usage, is an investigator hired for inquiries.

clue.text: Go ahead with borrowed money

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to move forward
as a noun, a loan or payment made before it is due

explanation.surface: Proceed with a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to move forward; the noun is money lent or paid early.

clue.text: Pride may come before, but what comes after a fall?

definitions.text: Pride may come before, but what comes after a fall?

parts.words: Pride may come before, but what comes after a fall?
parts.note: playing on the proverb 'pride comes before a fall', with fall in its American sense of autumn

explanation.surface: Twists the proverb 'pride goes before a fall' into a question.
explanation.walkthrough: Fall is the American word for autumn; the season that follows it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The coldest season of the year follows autumn, which Americans call fall.

clue.text: Replace points in part of car engine

indicators.note: to replace the letters is to put them back in different places

explanation.surface: A mechanic's instruction to fit new contact points in a car's motor.
explanation.walkthrough: Points were part of older ignition systems, so 'replace points' reads as a servicing task.
explanation.definitionFit: The sliding cylinder driven by combustion inside an engine's cylinder is a core component.

clue.text: I've an alternative that's simple

indicators.note: an alternative version of the letters is a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have an easy other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' rearranges IVE AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple, unsophisticated person is innocent and credulous, a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Old coach station

definitions.meaning: a light four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage of the nineteenth century
a major London railway terminus, also home to London's main coach station

explanation.surface: Reads as a coach station for long-distance buses.
explanation.walkthrough: VICTORIA is a London railway terminus, beside the city's main long-distance coach station.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a low horse-drawn carriage, and of a big London rail terminus.

clue.text: An ear, perhaps — for music?

definitions.meaning: a body part with a function, such as the ear, is an example
a keyboard instrument with pipes, played in churches

explanation.surface: Asks whether one's hearing is meant for music.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear is a body part with a function; a pipe instrument is played for music.

clue.text: Authorise coercive measure

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to give official permission
as a noun, a penalty imposed to force compliance

explanation.surface: Approving a forceful policy.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two nearly opposite senses: approval and penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to approve officially; the noun is a penalty such as a trade embargo.

clue.text: Powerful Russian fighter gains height reaching capital of Yemen

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A Russian jet climbs as it approaches the Yemeni capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Yemen' suggests Sanaa, but it gives only the first letter, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very strong or forceful has great power, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Venerate an American patriot

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to respect deeply
Paul ..., who rode to warn of British troops in 1775

explanation.surface: Honour a hero of the American Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere is famous for his midnight ride warning that British troops were coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to hold in deep respect; it is also the surname of the Revolutionary rider.

clue.text: Girl holds chap back somewhere in Denmark

indicators.note: holds means the girl's name contains the other piece
back means the man's name is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A woman is holding a man back at some Danish location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds chap back' reads as restraining a man; 'back' reverses the name, which 'holds' then puts inside the girl's name. Elsinore is Hamlet's setting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Danish port of Helsingor, setting of Hamlet's castle, is known in English by this name.
